summary.headline: eClerx Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 10.6% YoY to USD 127.7M, but deal wins fell to USD 31M and ACV dropped about 10% YoY in H1.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue was USD 127.7M (up 10.6% YoY, 12.9% in constant currency, up 1.5% QoQ), marking the 13th straight quarter of sequential growth. Operating EBITDA margin rose 90 bps QoQ to 23.9%, which management attributed almost entirely to INR depreciation (FX), while H1 margin ran about 190 bps below last year as the company invests in new locations and AI. New deal wins were USD 31M versus USD 41M in Q1, and management said clients are delaying decisions and starting with smaller AI-led pilots. Management reiterated a 24% to 28% full-year EBITDA margin range but conceded that restoring full-year ACV to FY26 levels will be difficult.

segments.name: Analytics and Automation
segments.commentary: Grew 5% QoQ and 27% YoY, about twice company growth; annual run rate about USD 109M, roughly 20% of revenue. Technology team of 2,300 people.

segments.name: Emerging business
segments.commentary: Now 12.6% of revenue, up from 11.7%; growth led by finance and accounting (FinOps) and mix of advertising, logistics and shipping clients.

segments.name: Communication, Media and Telecom
segments.commentary: Broadly flat QoQ; Cairo and Manila growing, new voice programs ramping, QA 360 deployed at a large client.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew about 3% QoQ on short-term engagements; US easing of financial crime compliance rules cut refresh volumes at existing clients; new AML/KYC work with a payments company.

segments.name: Hi-tech and Manufacturing & Distribution
segments.commentary: Traction in Hi-tech from agentic AI and transformation services; Fashion, luxury and retail flat YoY, with Q2 seasonally weak due to Italy August holidays and weak China and Europe luxury demand.

guidance_outlook: Full-year operating EBITDA margin expected within the 24% to 28% range; management said it remains confident of this range.
H2 margin headwind of about 20 bps from the revised statutory PF wage ceiling (INR 15,000 to INR 25,000 per month, effective September 17, 2026).
D&A including Ind AS 116 rent expected to rise about 20 bps in H2 as Mumbai and Pune facilities come live in Q3 and Q4.
H2 CapEx expected roughly equal to H1 (about INR 90 crore per half), not double.
Next year CapEx expected to be lower as seat additions slow to about 800 to 1,000 over the next couple of quarters, subject to budgeting.
Management aims to match FY26 ACV for the full year but said it will be difficult; BFSI recovery now expected in Q4 rather than Q3.
capex_capacity: H1 CapEx INR 919M; Q2 INR 585M. H2 CapEx guided roughly equal to H1.
India seat count up about 1,400 to 16,824 as Mohali and Chandigarh capacity went live.
Additional seats coming in Mumbai and Pune in H2; new facilities driving higher depreciation.
Next year seat additions expected to be lower, about 800 to 1,000 over the next couple of quarters.
demand_pricing: Deal wins USD 31M in Q2 vs USD 41M in Q1; H1 USD 72M vs USD 78M prior year.
H1 ACV about INR 72M, down about 10% YoY; management says clients are delaying decisions and starting with smaller AI pilots, not because of competitive pressure.
Management said there is a shift-right in deals and Q2 bench was higher than usual because of it; headcount was added ahead of expected work.
Roll-off in Q1 and Q2 at about 15% to 20% of revenue, in line with the usual range.
Management denied losing BFSI market share and cited US regulatory easing and AI adoption in FCC work as the causes of softness.

qa_highlights.question: Are deal sizes and decision timelines shrinking, and how is ACV trending?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 ACV about INR 72M, about 10% below prior year. Clients are taking longer and starting with smaller AI pilots; management still aims to match FY26 ACV but said it will be difficult.

qa_highlights.question: How will EBITDA margin trend for the full year, and is nearshore mix a drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin depends on revenue growth. Nearshore centres (Philippines, Egypt, etc.) carry lower margins than India, which dilutes the mix, but each centre is improving; the 24% to 28% full-year range is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CapEx outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 CapEx roughly equal to H1 at about INR 90 crore per half, not double. Next year's CapEx expected to be lower as seat additions slow.

qa_highlights.question: Is BFSI losing share, and when does recovery come?
qa_highlights.answer: No share loss per management. Recovery now expected in Q4 rather than Q3, helped by adjacent areas such as payments KYC/AML and mortgages.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company going to pursue acquisitions to accelerate growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital is not the constraint. Target assets must be synergistic and culturally aligned; healthcare is an area under review as valuations have eased. Management has not yet closed a deal.

qa_highlights.question: Why is headcount up 3.5% QoQ when ACV is weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount was added in advance of work that has not yet materialized because of the shift-right, which lowered utilization to 74.9%.

risks_watch: Deal wins and ACV continue to decline; Q3 and Q4 need about USD 49M to 50M per quarter just to hold flat ACV.
Utilization at 74.9% and attrition at 23.4% with headcount outpacing revenue.
BFSI volume pressure from easing US financial crime compliance rules; recovery now pushed to Q4.
AI-led client budget cuts and deflation pass-through, especially in top 10 clients (growth in mid-single digits).
Margin pressure from nearshore mix, PF wage ceiling change (20 bps) and higher D&A (about 20 bps more in H2).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term AI and domain strategy and on margin delivery, but cautious and candid on the short term: management repeatedly said decisions are slower, ACV is down and FY26 ACV matching will be difficult. Some answers on AI deal economics and renewal exposure were non-specific and deferred to later follow-up.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: Deal wins and ACV recovery to FY26 levels
